newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler seen doubling first half profit.
newsitem.headline: Daimler seen doubling first half profit.

text.p: Daimler-Benz AG is likely to show net profit more than doubled in the first half of this year when the industrial conglomorate holds its annual mid-year press conference in London on Thursday.

Daimler, which like nearly all German export-dependent firms, stands to get a big lift from the strong dollar and should show improvements in all major operating units which face strict internal profitability goals.

Analysts said on average they expected Daimler to show group net profit climbed to around two billion marks in the first half of 1997 compared with 827 million marks during the first half of 1996 and that sales should climb to around 56 billion marks from 49.07 billion marks a year ago.

"All in all, I expect very, very cheery numbers from the Daimler press conference," said Peter Schmidt, analyst at Automotive Industry Data outside London. "Daimler could show a significant improvement in the figures."
In the first four months of this year, Daimler sales appeared to support such remarks, climbing 15 percent to 36.3 billion marks.
The predicted sales growth comes as Daimler is making big strides toward reducing costs and making itself more efficient in the world market place.
As of April 1, Daimler's car and truck making unit, Mercedes-Benz AG was merged into the corporate structure in an effort to speed up decision making and cut overheads.
As has been the case since Daimler started recovering from a record loss of more than seven billion marks in 1995, profit growth will come largely from Mercedes.

Analysts said there was no question that Mercedes cars will show continued strong sales growth, coming largely from the U.S. and on the back of models such as the SLK roadster and the E-Class executive class saloon.

Many, however, will be paying close attention to comments Daimler executives might make about the new A-Class model which hits showrooms this fall and the tiny "Swatch" car, due out in Europe by next spring.
Both represent an unprecedented move by Daimler into small cars and are thought expensive to develop because they do not rely on an existing Mercedes base platform.

With sales of Mercedes cars hitting records, analysts will focus on heavy trucks which have suffered from a weak market, but appear to be recovering following the introduction of a new range of models last year.
"We will be looking to see that things are going better with heavy trucks," said Georg Stuerzer, analyst at Vereinsbank in Munich.

Daimler's other major unit, Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (DASA), meanwhile is also expected to report solid progress toward returning toward profitability as painful cost-cutting and reorganisations at the unit begin to bear fruit.
DASA, which lost 700 million marks in the first half of 1996, is expected to have received a big lift from the dollar and improved orders at the Airbus consortium in which DASA is a major partner.
The aircraft unit has proven worryingly vulnerable to swings in the dollar in recent years because most aircraft orders are denominated in the U.S. currency.

But with the dollar up roughly 20 percent against the mark so far this year, DASA could reap an unexpected windfall depending on what extent the company had isolated itself from currency swings with hedging.
"DASA will make a clear move back to the profit zone," said Klaus-Juergen Melzner, analyst at Deutsche Bank.

Analysts also expect Daimler's information technology unit, Debis, to showed continued solid profit growth, but proceeds from the sale of its stake in Cap Gemini will not be felt until the second half of this year.
Analysts said assuming the half year figures come in as expected, Daimler should report net profit for 1997 as a whole of around four billion marks and sales of 115 billion to 117 billion marks.
